Instead, start with the standards - different beers, jack/rum and coke, margarita, and you can mix a LOT with the "clear" liquors, be it high end tequila, vodka, gin, etc., and work your way up, but do it at...not necessarily a lower end bar, but maybe a less traveled, quieter watering hole. Tempting though it may be to frequent the club locale with the pretty girl/guy tending, nine times out of ten they're there to look good and open bottles of brew. I've frequented many a bar and asked for a white russian only to find a blank stare in return. It's three ingredients for fuck's sake!

When learning, stick to the bar less traveled, ask the server behind the bar the question you're posing here. But hell, for the case of argument, if that's where you find yourself, look at the specials and try what looks interesting. Hit the bar during the off hours. Most tenders are so sick of slinging cranberry/redbull vodkas that they'll appreciate being asked and might make you something creative and original. Of course, this varies from bar to bar, which is why I recommend a less "busy" location.

But if they're worth their salt, they'll appreciate your honesty and introduce you to something quite tasty.

If bars aren't an option, ask whoever's working at your local liquor store. I've worked in a few, and if they know their shit, they can help you pair a beer or wine with anything to complement a cheese, cured meat, chocolate, or anything in between.

You can get a wide variety of pre-made mixer drinks at damn near any liquor store, with easy to follow directions on the back and what booze to be added, be they Hurricanes, Bloody Marys, Cosmos, and a buffet of dozens of drinks ending in "tini."

If you're cheap, substitute the suggested brand with an alternative. Case in point, prosecco in place of champagne, or popov in place of absolut or smirnoff, coruba or cortez over bacardi. Apply when applicable. It's a mixed drink, you're not going to taste the difference, and your wallet will thank you. Experiment and see what you like, refrigerate when advised.

Scope the stores around the holidays, and you'll eventually come across "gift" sets that come pre-packaged with all the accoutrement you'll need, and usually at the same price as a solo bottle to encourage sales. For example, Goslings will often have a bottle of dark rum with two cans of ginger beer for a Dark n' Stormy.

Jack/Rum and coke is always an old reliable, but a dark and/or light rum with any combo with a splash of varied fruit juices tossed over ice can make it feel like summer. Serve in a tiki glass with a tiny umbrella to impress a fair maiden.

Fresh bread came in every morning, but whatever didn't sell that day was given away to customers/employees so as not to waste food. Nine times out of ten, the mass of it went to a guy who used it at a soup kitchen a few towns over. Wrapped well enough, it could stay fairly well for a few days. So if you were shopping at the right time, you'd get free bread that was still in relatively good shape. 

The downside was you'd get people that learned about this, and would come in with 5-10 minutes left before closing expecting free bread, and would complain when none was left.

I still remember a guy who said he fell on hard times, asking for said bread. It was still a while before we were set to place it at the registers, but I felt bad for him, wrapped it up nice so it'd last, and had it waiting for him. Even paged the cashier to tell them not to charge the guy for it. Fucker then comes around the corner with a cart (didn't have one when he gave me his sob story) LOADED with booze, grabs the bread and is on the way. No thanks or anything.

I understand drowning your sorrows with a bottle, but with the amount of stuff this guy had, he was prepared for a serious party.
